## Pull request overview

Adds opt-in navigation enhancements to `@object-ui/layout`’s schema-driven sidebar, extending `NavigationRenderer`/`AppSchemaRenderer` with search filtering, pin-to-favorites, and drag reorder support.

**Changes:**
- Added `searchQuery`, pinning callbacks, and drag-reorder plumbing (via `@dnd-kit`) to `NavigationRenderer`, plus exported `filterNavigationItems()`.
- Wired a sidebar search input in `AppSchemaRenderer` and forwarded pin/reorder props to the internal sidebar navigation.
- Expanded layout test coverage for search/pin/reorder behavior and updated the roadmap status.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 6 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.

| `packages/layout/src/__tests__/NavigationRenderer.test.tsx` | Adds tests for search filtering, pinning/favorites, and reorder. |
| `packages/layout/src/__tests__/AppSchemaRenderer.test.tsx` | Adds tests for sidebar search wiring and pin/reorder prop forwarding. |
| `packages/layout/package.json` | Adds `@dnd-kit/*` dependencies to the layout package. |

`enableReorder` is only applied in the `!hasGroups` branch. When the navigation contains groups, the renderer never wraps items in a `DndContext` / `SortableContext` and never passes drag listeners down, so drag-reorder is effectively ignored for grouped navigation trees. If reorder is intended to work with groups too, extend the DnD wiring to the mixed/grouped rendering path (e.g., per group/leaf buffer) and add coverage for that case; otherwise, consider explicitly disabling/hiding reorder when `hasGroups` is true to avoid a silently non-functional prop.

Reorder UI is gated only on `enableReorder`, not on `onReorder`. If a consumer enables reorder but omits `onReorder`, items become draggable but the updated order is never emitted/persisted. Consider enabling drag handles / sortable behavior only when both `enableReorder` and `onReorder` are provided (similar to the `enablePinning && onPinToggle` guard used for pinning).

The drag handle is rendered as a non-focusable `<span>` with `...dragListeners`. Since `KeyboardSensor` is registered, this setup blocks keyboard-initiated reordering (the activator can’t receive focus/keydown), and the span also lacks the draggable ARIA `attributes`. Consider rendering the handle as a focusable button and wiring `useSortable`’s activator (`setActivatorNodeRef`) + `attributes`/`listeners` to that element.
```suggestion
          <button
            type="button"
            className="absolute left-0.5 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 cursor-grab text-muted-foreground"
            aria-label="Drag to reorder"
            {...dragListeners}
          >
            <LucideIcons.GripVertical className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
          </button>
```

Same issue as the action-item path: the reorder handle is a non-focusable `<span>` with `...dragListeners`, which prevents keyboard-initiated reordering when `KeyboardSensor` is enabled and omits the draggable ARIA `attributes` from the handle. Consider using a focusable button activator (with `setActivatorNodeRef`) so drag-reorder is accessible.
```suggestion
        <button
          type="button"
          className="absolute left-0.5 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 cursor-grab text-muted-foreground"
          aria-label="Drag to reorder"
          {...dragListeners}
        >
          <LucideIcons.GripVertical className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
        </button>
```

`@object-ui/layout` is the “Shell” package, and the repo’s architecture guide calls out that heavy 3rd‑party dependencies should live in `@object-ui/plugin-*` packages (see `.github/copilot-instructions.md` monorepo topology table). Adding `@dnd-kit/*` directly to layout will increase the baseline bundle for every consumer, even when `enableReorder` is not used. Consider isolating reorder into a lazily-loaded subcomponent/module (loaded only when enabled) or moving the feature behind a plugin-style boundary to keep the layout package lightweight.
